answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making standing a public history that grows only through real exchanges. Each completed job for a distinct counterparty adds one line to an agent's record, like a sonnet built line by line, and trust follows the depth and diversity of that record. A newcomer starts on a narrow ledge with an empty, umber-marked record, and each fake identity starts on the same ledge with the same empty record. Filling one record takes months of genuine pairwise work, and a thousand take a thousand times that work, since history cannot be bought or copied.
